The width is still tied to viewport\n         height, but only to keep the chart a sensible size -- nothing depends\n         on guessing the chrome, and being wrong now costs a scrollbar rather\n         than spilled content.\n\n         The chart keeps its exact aspect ratio deliberately. It is drawn with\n         preserveAspectRatio=\"none\", so constraining its height instead would\n         stretch every axis label horizontally. */\n      dialog.expanded {\n        box-sizing: border-box;\n        width: min(96vw, calc(78vh * 2.3684210526315788), 1700px);\n        max-width: 96vw;\n        /* vh is the *large* viewport: on a phone it includes the strip behind\n           a retracted URL bar, so a dialog sized in vh can sit partly under\n           browser chrome. dvh tracks what is actually visible. The vh line is\n           the fallback for engines without dvh, and is no worse than the\n           unbounded height this replaced. */\n        max-height: 92vh;\n        max-height: 92dvh;\n        display: flex;\n        flex-direction: column;\n        border: none; border-radius: 12px; padding: 16px;\n        background: var(--hpo-surface, #ffffff);\n        color: var(--hpo-text, #212121);\n        box-shadow: 0 8px 32px rgba(0,0,0,0.35);\n        overflow: hidden;\n      }\n      .dlg-body {\n        flex: 1 1 auto;\n        min-height: 0;\n        overflow-y: auto;\n        /* R7-D4-01 (#1454): a width:100% table whose min-content width\n           exceeds this box overflows it, and hidden put that overflow\n           outside every gesture -- the savings table's right-aligned percent\n           column was the instance, painted where no scroll could reach it.\n           auto reaches it instead, and costs nothing at a width where\n           nothing overflows. */\n        overflow-x: auto;\n        /* Room for the scrollbar so it never lands on top of the chart. */\n        scrollbar-gutter: stable;\n      }\n      dialog.expanded::backdrop {\n        background: rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.55);\n      }\n      .dlg-head {\n        display: flex; An outline on an SVG rect is painted around the element's box in the viewport, where the row's neighbours and the diagram's edges cut it: the reporter saw a ring with only its top and left sides left. Once the real chrome passed the budget the content ran past the dialog's painted background instead of being contained -- 449px past it at 1400x700, measured.
